subject: Consecutive-window availability for technical deep dive & rotating coverage
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Consecutive-window availability for technical deep dive & rotating coverage

Hi Samuel — thanks again for the discovery call this morning. Really helpful to hear about Cardinal Health's latency targets and the multi-region routing constraints for your patient-facing workflows.

Quick recap and ask: we recommended a 60–75 minute technical deep dive with one of our solutions engineers to walk through the model routing, cache strategies, and security posture (KMS/Network). To make it easy for your global team, we can run a consecutive-window series: three short consecutive weekly windows that rotate the time-of-day so your US/EU/APAC engineers each get at least one session in their local business hours.

Proposed approach (examples below are in UTC and local equivalents):
- Option A (single 75-min deep dive): Week of Oct 18, Wed 75-min session at 15:00–16:15 UTC
  - US (ET): 11:00–12:15
  - EU (BST): 16:00–17:15
  - APAC (SGT): 23:00–00:15 (late for APAC)
- Option B (consecutive-window rotation): Three 45-min sessions on successive weeks rotating start times so each region gets a friendly slot
  - Week 1 (US-friendly): 15:00 UTC / 11:00 ET / 16:00 BST / 23:00 SGT
  - Week 2 (EU-friendly): 09:00 UTC / 05:00 ET / 10:00 BST / 17:00 SGT
  - Week 3 (APAC-friendly): 00:00 UTC / 20:00 ET / 01:00 BST / 08:00 SGT

If you prefer a single focused meeting, we can cover everything in a 75-min deep dive with a follow-up office hours slot for APAC; if you want broader participation across teams, the consecutive-window rotation usually works well to reduce late-night attendance.

Please let me know: 1) which option you prefer; 2) a couple of dates/times that work for your engineering leads (we can send calendar invites and include a lightweight agenda). I attached a suggested agenda and our one-pager for context.

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0129

Attachments: redwood-technical-deep-dive-agenda.pdf (PDF, 1pg), redwood-onepager.pdf (PDF, 2pg)

From: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@cardinalhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@cardinalhealth.com>, Cardinal Health Eng <eng-infra@cardinalhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T10:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Consecutive-window availability for technical deep dive & rotating coverage

Thanks Naomi — great summary. Priya and I reviewed this and we like the consecutive-window rotation idea so our regional teams can attend at least one session in-hours. A couple notes from our side:
- We prefer 45-min technical sessions (tight agenda) + 30-min optional office hours the following day for follow-up questions.
- Our infra lead (eng-infra@cardinalhealth.com) will want to see network/topology discussion and we will ask our security team if they want a separate follow-up for compliance artifacts.

Availability windows (for US/EU leads):
- Week of Oct 18: Tue/Fri mornings ET (09:00–12:00 ET) — US-friendly week
- Week of Oct 25: Tue/Thu late mornings BST (10:00–13:00 BST) — EU-friendly week
- Week of Nov 1: Tue/Thu mornings SGT (09:00–12:00 SGT) — APAC-friendly week

Can you propose three concrete 45-min slots (one in each week) and we'll confirm with the regional leads? Also please include who from Redwood will present (SE + solutions AE).

Samuel Ortiz
Principal Product Manager — Digital Enablement
Cardinal Health
samuel.ortiz@cardinalhealth.com

On a practical note: prefer invites in UTC timestamps so our calendar rotations are consistent.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@cardinalhealth.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Consecutive-window availability for technical deep dive & rotating coverage

Hey Samuel — Marcus from Redwood SE here. Happy to lead the technical sessions. Proposed concrete 45-min slots in UTC (one per requested week):

- US-friendly week (Week of Oct 18): 2026-10-19 15:00–15:45 UTC (11:00–11:45 ET)
- EU-friendly week (Week of Oct 25): 2026-10-26 09:30–10:15 UTC (10:30–11:15 BST)
- APAC-friendly week (Week of Nov 1): 2026-11-02 00:30–01:15 UTC (08:30–09:15 SGT)

Agenda (45 min):
1) Quick recap & goals (5)
2) Architecture walk (routing, caching, model variants) (20)
3) Security/network callouts (KMS, VPC options) (10)
4) Next steps & office hours scheduling (10)

We can run the APAC slot earlier/later if 00:30–01:15 UTC is uncomfortable — that one is flexible. For the follow-up office hours, we suggest a 30-min block the following business day in the same region's local hours (we'll propose when confirmed).

Can Naomi send calendar invites in UTC and include the lightweight agenda + link to the one-pager? Also, do you have a preferred conferencing platform (we can use your Teams link or send a Google Meet).

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: sample-infra-drawing.png (image stub)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T11:05:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Consecutive-window availability for technical deep dive & rotating coverage

Perfect — thanks everyone. Confirming the three slots Marcus suggested; I'll send three separate calendar invites (UTC times) labeled: "Cardinal Health — Tech Deep Dive (US-friendly)", "... (EU-friendly)", "... (APAC-friendly)" and include Marcus as presenter plus Logan for account context.

Quick checklist before invites go out:
- Samuel / Priya: please confirm the attendee list for each session (we'll include eng-infra@cardinalhealth.com but name primary contacts if you want pre-assigned breakout items).
- Security artifacts: if your compliance team wants the SOC/architecture evidence ahead of the EU session, we can share our evidence package (PDF) — let me know and we'll attach it to the invite.
- Conferencing: we'll send Google Meet links by default unless you provide a Teams URL.

I'll also attach the one-pager and agenda to each invite and drop the HubSpot deal link in the description. Expect invites within 2 hours.

Best — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

Related links: https://hubspot.example/deal/DEAL-3492
